$documentation: Enumerated exceptions for the blocking dependency-audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs,
run by the `audit` job in .github/workflows/test.yml). Policy narrative lives in
Every advisory `bun audit` reports must either be FIXED or appear here. There is no
third option and no global escape hatch: this file replaced a `continue-on-error` +
`|| echo` pair whose justification ('all in harper transitive deps') was true when it
was written, carried no expiry, and was still silently passing the build long after it
Adding an entry is a REVIEWED act, not a way to get green. Each one must carry the
advisory id, what pulls it in, why it cannot be fixed from this repo, a hard expiry
date, and the concrete condition that retires it. The gate enforces all of that
mechanically, including a severity-scaled cap on how long an entry may live — you
cannot park a critical for a year.
When an entry expires the build FAILS and a human re-decides. That is the mechanism
working. Re-dating an entry without re-reading its reason is how this file rots back

classes.no-patch-published: No fixed version exists on the registry yet. Verified by the gate on every run: if a patched version ships, this entry fails and must be actioned.
classes.vendor-pinned: A patched version exists upstream, but the vulnerable copy is resolved inside a vendored dependency whose tree we do not control. Retired by moving the vendor, not by bumping the leaf.
classes.remediation-available: A patched version exists AND we could take it. Deliberately deferred to a separate, test-gated dependency PR so a security gate lands independently of a lockfile change. Shortest leash of the three.

entries.reason: Renewed 2026-10-22 after re-reading against harper 5.3.1; harper 5.3.3, the version flair pins (package.json:69), ships the same copies (first added 2026-07-27; renewed 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-07). Resolved copies: one in bun.lock (@fastify/static 9.3.0, pulled only by harper ^9.1.3) and harper 5.3.3's bundled copy 9.3.0 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/@fastify/static in npm and bun installs of flair). The fix is 10.1.1 (10.1.2 for GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj; npm's latest is 10.1.7), and the 9.x line ends at 9.3.0 with no backport. Every harper release inspected still declares ^9.1.3 (5.3.1; 5.3.3, latest; 5.3.2; 5.2.15, latest-5.2; 5.1.29, latest-5.1; 5.3.0-beta.4, next), so the fix is a major bump inside harper's HTTP layer that a root override would force on the server harper itself mounts. Where it is used: harper 5.3.3 imports it only in dist/server/operationsServer.js:53 and registers it once (:208), on the operations server, with a fixed root of harper's own Studio assets (studio/web); flair's localStudio enabled: false (src/commands/init.ts:1039,1194) changes only which page the / handler serves (:209-215), not that registration. That file adds no request hook of its own; authentication on the operations server is per-route preValidation (GET /api/openapi/rest :217, POST / :220, and the operations MCP route at :194-203, registered only when mcp.operations is configured, which flair does not set), so no guard is tied to the paths the plugin serves. harper's application-port static handler uses send, not this plugin (dist/server/static.js:12), and flair's component config declares no static handler (config.yaml). flair does not import @fastify/static. The default flair install binds the operations server to 127.0.0.1 (src/cli.ts:578, resolved at :1882-1891) plus a domain socket (src/commands/init.ts:1026,1037) that is owner-only unless FLAIR_SOCKET_GROUP opts a group in (posture at src/cli.ts:2129-2147,2165-2173); an operator who widens the bind with --ops-bind or FLAIR_OPS_BIND makes the plugin reachable beyond loopback. Short leash (11 days), expiry aligned with the other harper-pinned high entries, pending the upstream move.
entries.removeWhen: flair moves to a harper release whose installed tree resolves @fastify/static >=10.1.1 (>=10.1.2 also retires GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj), whether pinned by its npm-shrinkwrap or shipped in its bundle; or flair stops depending on harper. As of 2026-10-22 no published harper release does: 5.3.3, 5.3.2, 5.3.1, 5.2.15, 5.1.29 and 5.3.0-beta.4 all declare ^9.1.3, and the 9.x line ends at 9.3.0.

entries.reason: O(depth-squared) event-loop DoS in stream-json's pick/ignore/filter/replace filters on crafted nested JSON. stream-json@1.9.1 is a bundled copy inside harper (@harperfast/harper; harper 5.3.3); it cannot be overridden from this repo (harper ships the copy in its installed tree, where a root override does not reach in npm or bun installs, flair#1498/#1510). flair does not import stream-json directly - reachability is only via harper's internal streaming parser, not flair code.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json > 3.4.0 (the patched line), or flair stops depending on harper.

entries.reason: Prototype pollution in stream-json's Assembler (fixed in 3.6.0). Harper 5.3.3 ships stream-json 1.9.1 as a bundled copy, which a root override does not reach in npm or bun installs (flair#1498/#1510). A Bun root override to stream-json 3.x is deferred pending compatibility testing. flair does not import stream-json. Harper 5.3.3 imports StreamArray and Batch in dist/dataLayer/bulkLoad.js; its import_from_s3 operation selects JSON from the S3 object's extension. StreamArray builds each element through the Assembler, so that path is in scope; Harper checks target-table insert permission for an insert import, update permission for update, and both for upsert (dist/utility/operation_authorization.js).
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json >= 3.6.0, or flair stops depending on harper.

entries.reason: Quadratic re-scan in stream-json's JSONC parser and verifier (fixed after 3.5.0). The installed stream-json 1.9.1 package ships no JSONC parser. Harper 5.3.3 ships stream-json 1.9.1 as a bundled copy, which a root override does not reach in npm or bun installs (flair#1498/#1510). A Bun root override to stream-json 3.x is deferred pending compatibility testing. flair does not import stream-json. Harper 5.3.3 imports StreamArray and Batch in dist/dataLayer/bulkLoad.js; its import_from_s3 operation selects JSON from the S3 object's extension.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json > 3.5.0, or flair stops depending on harper; re-check this entry if harper moves to a stream-json major that includes the JSONC parser.

entries.reason: Renewed 2026-10-07 after re-reading against harper 5.2.8, the version flair then pinned; harper 5.3.3 ships the same copy (first added 2026-10-02). No fixed release exists: npm's latest node-forge is 1.4.0, inside the affected range (<=1.4.0). Resolved copies: one in bun.lock (node-forge 1.4.0, pulled only by harper ^1.3.1) and harper 5.3.3's bundled copy 1.4.0 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/node-forge in npm and bun installs of flair); 5.3.3 declares ^1.3.1. flair's own code does not import it. harper 5.3.3's only import is node_modules/harper/dist/security/keys.js:64, which uses forge.pki to create and sign its CA and server certificates (generateCertificates :543-567, generateCertAuthority :589-613) and to parse and PEM-encode keys and certificates (:491, :538-539, :547, :617, :649, :689, :695, :706, :708). keys.js never calls node-forge's RSA signature verification, the path this advisory affects. As a no-patch-published entry, the gate blocks it once npm's latest node-forge is outside the affected range (when the audit can reach the registry). Expiry aligned with the other harper-pinned high entries.
entries.removeWhen: npm's latest node-forge release is outside the affected range (the gate then blocks this entry): reassess; a maintainer removes the entry once harper resolves a fixed release or drops node-forge

entries.reason: Resolved inside @google/adk's own tree, which we do not control: @google/adk 2.2.1 depends on @google-cloud/vertexai ^1.12.0, which requires google-auth-library ^9; google-auth-library requires gaxios, and gaxios requires uuid ^9.0.1. uuid 9.0.1 is in this advisory's affected range (<11.1.1). A direct dependency or override in @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair cannot reach it (npm resolves the nested copy under gaxios), and the ADK consumer install confirms the vulnerable copy is still present. flair's adapter does not import uuid. Retired when @google/adk's tree resolves uuid outside the affected range.
entries.removeWhen: a @google/adk release's dependency tree resolves uuid >= 11.1.1 (its @google-cloud/vertexai -> google-auth-library -> gaxios edge moves off uuid 9.x), or the ADK consumer install no longer reports this advisory

entries.reason: Published 2026-10-23; URI scheme spoofing via percent-encoded scheme decoding. Resolved inside harper's installed tree, which neither npm nor bun reaches with a root override: harper 5.3.3, the version flair pins (package.json:69), bundles fast-uri 3.1.0 at node_modules/harper/node_modules/fast-uri and 4.2.1 at node_modules/harper/node_modules/fastify/node_modules/fast-json-stringify/node_modules/fast-uri in npm and bun installs of flair. The root override (fast-uri 4.2.3) keeps flair's own tree on the fixed 4.x, but harper's runtime loads its bundled copies too. flair does not import fast-uri; the copies in an npm install of the flair package are harper's, reached through its fastify stack. Fixed in 3.1.9 (3.x) and 4.2.3 (4.x); both bundled copies are affected.
entries.removeWhen: flair moves to a harper release whose installed tree resolves fast-uri >=3.1.9 on the 3.x line and >=4.2.3 on the 4.x line, or flair stops depending on harper.
